title: Judah's plea (Genesis 44:18–34)
hook: Judah offers himself as a slave in Benjamin's place

segments.voice: Yesterday, the silver cup: the same chance to abandon a favorite son, and the brothers refused. Your line was not this time. Today, the brother who once said sell him steps forward. Day seventy-three.

Picture the room. The governor of Egypt, the most powerful man any of them has ever met, has just said: the one with the cup stays as my slave, the rest of you go. The brothers are on the floor. Benjamin is standing there, the cup found in his bag, his whole life about to be taken away. And the Torah says: "Then Judah came near unto him." In Hebrew, one word, vayigash, and he drew near. Nobody tells him to. Nobody expects him to. Judah, who years ago looked at another brother in a pit and said, let's sell him, walks up to the most dangerous man in the room. Today: what he says.
screen: `THE ONE WITH THE CUP STAYS.` → `THEN JUDAH CAME NEAR.` → `THE BROTHER WHO SAID SELL HIM.`

segments.voice: Judah's speech is one of the longest in the book of Genesis, and it isn't clever. It's a story. He tells the governor about their old father. About the son of his old age, whose brother is dead, the only one left from his mother, and whom his father loves. He quotes his father's own words: you know my wife bore me two sons; one went out from me, and I said, surely he is torn in pieces, and I haven't seen him since. If you take this one too, and harm comes to him, you'll bring my gray hairs down with sorrow to the grave. Listen to what Judah is doing. He's saying out loud that his father loves Benjamin more. He's accepting it. The jealousy that sold Joseph is gone. And then the offer: "let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren." Take me instead. I'll be your slave for the rest of my life. And the last line: "For how shall I go up to my father, if the lad be not with me?" Think about who's hearing this. Joseph. The brother who was sold into slavery is now listening to the man who sold him offer to become a slave, so that a brother, and a father, won't suffer what Joseph and Jacob suffered. The rabbis honor Judah as the model of turning around, teshuvah. And the Jewish people came to be named after him: Judah, Yehudah, gave us the word Jew.
screen: `VAYIGASH: AND HE DREW NEAR.` · `OUR FATHER LOVES HIM.` · `LET ME STAY INSTEAD OF THE LAD.` · `JUDAH, YEHUDAH, JEW.` · then, large: `HOW SHALL I GO UP TO MY FATHER?`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: offer to carry someone's load. Settle, and breathe. Think of someone near you who's carrying too much right now. A parent with a sick kid. A friend in a hard month. A coworker buried in work. Think of one concrete thing you could take off their hands. A meal, a ride, a shift, an afternoon of childcare. Not a vague let me know. A real offer. Decide who and what. The bell holds the time.
Judah's plea. The brother who once said sell him draws near and offers himself as a slave, so that Benjamin can go home.
Your line: take me instead. Today, make one real offer to carry something for someone, and mean it. Day seventy-three.

howItsDone: Judah's plea opens the weekly Torah portion Vayigash, read in synagogue each winter, and Jewish teaching holds him up as the model of someone who truly changed.

pairs: the name behind the word Jew

myth: Judah argued that Benjamin was innocent
he didn't argue about the cup. he told the story of their father and offered himself instead.
the word Jew comes from Judah's name
Yehudah, Judah; the tribe and later the kingdom of Judah gave the people their name.
Judah was the brother who suggested selling Joseph
in Genesis 37 he said, let's sell him. here he offers himself as a slave.

fork.setup: you're Judah. you promised your father you'd bring Benjamin home. now the governor says Benjamin stays as a slave. what do you do?
options: go home and tell your father the truth.
offer to stay as a slave in his place.
try to steal Benjamin back at night.
fork.reveal: he draws near and offers himself: let me stay instead of the lad. it's the speech that breaks Joseph open.

original.note: Hebrew: and he drew near. the first word of Judah's plea, and the name of the Torah portion.

trapdoor: what you thought: a brother pleading for mercy.
what it means: the man who sold one brother offers his own freedom to save another. that's how change is proved.
what a scholar hears: vayigash, 44:18, opens the portion. Judah had pledged himself as surety for Benjamin (43:9), and now pays it.
